name: Cacheu fort and trading post
subtitle: Cacheu, on the coast of Guinea-Bissau, was a Portuguese trading post where, in AFP's words, millions of enslaved people saw West Africa for the last time.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: A Portuguese trading post on the coast

facts.label: Population and past status
facts.value: Fewer than 10,000 people today; capital of the Portuguese colony from the 16th century, trading in people until the late 19th century

facts.label: Present fort
facts.value: Built from 1641 by captain-major Gonçalo Gambôa de Ayalla against Spanish ships; still unfinished in 1647 (citing Teixeira 2010)

facts.label: Memorial
facts.value: Alfredo Caldeira of the Mario Soares foundation, which helped create the memorial, said Cacheu was the first place where Europeans practised transatlantic slavery on an industrial scale (his claim)

parts.text: Cacheu, on the coast of Guinea-Bissau, was a Portuguese trading post where, in AFP's words, millions of enslaved people saw West Africa for the last time. A thesis dates the town to 1588 and the present fort to 1641 to 1647. A memorial to slavery opened there in 2016.

gaps: The description is summarised from the sources listed here and should be read against them.
